long.description:
You're falling. Feet first, head last, straight toward the darkest thing in the universe — and in a few minutes you will cross a boundary from which nothing has ever returned. It blows my mind that the universe has a force so extreme it can unravel a human body atom by atom. In this episode of Cosmic Unknown, Captain Nova takes the fall with you: spaghettification, time slowing to a crawl, the event horizon, the singularity where physics gives up, Sagittarius A* in our own backyard, TON 618 at 66 billion suns, Hawking radiation, and the wild idea that black holes might be seeds of new universes. Sources woven through the episode: Einstein's general relativity, Hawking's 1974 evaporation work, and the Event Horizon Telescope's first black hole image (April 10, 2019).
